claims.text: Replacing a controlled fraction of heavier refractory elements with lighter oxide-forming elements reduces the alloy's density.
Substitution with lighter oxide-forming elements induces a dual-phase microstructure.
The induced microstructure consists of a robust intermetallic matrix and a continuous grain-boundary oxide film.
The modified microstructure maintains or slightly improves mechanical strength relative to the baseline alloy.
The modified alloy has greater corrosion resistance than the baseline alloy.
The modified alloy has greater high-temperature oxidation resistance than the baseline alloy.
Lighter oxide-forming elements promote formation of a continuous oxide film along grain boundaries.
The continuous grain-boundary oxide film limits oxygen penetration.
The continuous grain-boundary oxide film limits penetration by corrosive species.
The remaining intermetallic matrix pins dislocations.
The remaining intermetallic matrix provides mechanical support.
The proposed baseline alloy is predominantly composed of heavy refractory elements.
The proposed baseline alloy has a uniform single-phase microstructure.
The proposed baseline alloy lacks an engineered protective oxide framework.
An insufficient concentration of lighter oxide-forming elements will not produce a continuous protective oxide film.
An excessive concentration of lighter oxide-forming elements can cause over-oxidation and degrade mechanical integrity.
Processing or service environments that destabilize the dual-phase microstructure will cause the proposed performance relationship to cease to hold.
